scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. For his first two years he was dating another girl that I somewhat knew since we're in the same sorority but I wasn't close to. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the person in this scenario is the asshole (AITA) for lying to their boyfriend about his ex-girlfriend. Let me break this down step by step. First, the situation: They're college seniors, been dating for four months. The boyfriend was previously in a relationship with another girl, who they both knew through the sorority. They broke up because he suspected she was cheating based on rumors from a party. The person in question had a crush on him for a long time but knew he was in a relationship. When they started dating, he was still heartbroken and questioning the breakup. The person lied to him, saying she saw his ex with other guys at the party, which helped him move on faster. Now, he's happier and has no regrets. So, the question is: Is it right or wrong for her to lie, and why? I think the key points here are trust, honesty, and the impact of the lie on their relationship. Trust is fundamental in any relationship, and lying can erode that trust. Even if the intention was to help him feel better, lying is still a betrayal of trust. On the other hand, she might have felt that she was trying to help him move on and start a new chapter. She saw him in pain and wanted to alleviate that. But the problem is that lying, even with good intentions, can have consequences. If he ever finds out the truth, it could damage the relationship severely. Another angle is the potential for future issues. If she's willing to lie about something like this, it sets a precedent for dishonesty. It might make him question other things she says or does, even if they're unrelated. Also, the lie was about a past event that doesn't directly affect their current relationship. It's about his ex, not her. So, by lying, she's interfering with his ability to process his own emotions and past experiences. It's not healthy for him to move on based on a lie because it doesn't address the real issues. Furthermore, the fact that she's feeling guilty about it shows that she knows it's wrong. Guilt is a natural response to lying, and it's a sign that she should consider the implications of her actions. In conclusion, while her intentions might have been to help him, lying is not the right approach. It undermines trust and can lead to more problems down the line. It's better to be honest, even if it's difficult, because honesty builds a stronger foundation for the relationship.
